data.name: Tejeshwar
data.gender_notes: Tejeshwar is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.short_meaning: God of Fire, Lord of Power
data.long_meaning: Tej: Fire, Aasan: Seat, hence, One who sits on the Seat of Fire, the God of Fire. The name Tejeshwar carries the meaning “God of Fire, Lord of Power” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Tejeshwar usually hope their child will grow to embody god of fire, lord of power and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Tejeshwar symbolizes divine power, strength, and courage. It is believed that the name invokes the blessings of Lord Agni, the God of Fire, and bestows the wearer with the power to overcome all obstacles in life
data.etymology: Tejeshwar belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of Fire, Lord of Power.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Tejeshwar total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: The name Tejeshwar holds significant cultural importance in Hinduism, reflecting the reverence and honor held for the God of Fire, Agni. Agni is considered the messenger between the gods and humans, carrying offerings and prayers to the gods. The name Tejeshwar symbolizes the connection between the divine and mortal worlds, representing the power and purifying nature of fire. In various Hindu rituals and ceremonies, the name is chanted or invoked to bring blessings, success, and prosperity.
data.spiritual_significance: Tejeshwar is a spiritually empowering name, resonating with the inner fire of the soul. It symbolizes the power of the divine presence within us. The name inspires inner strength and resilience, just as the flame of a fire is unyielding and powerful. It also reminds us of the transformative and purifying nature of fire, which burns away impurities and negativity.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Tejeshwar: God of Sacred Fire. One who possesses the power of Tej or fiery energy.

historical_references.reference: Tejaswi, a legendary king of the Ikshvaku dynasty, is believed to have ruled around 1200 BCE. His name 'Tejaswi' is derived from Tejas, meaning radiance or splendor. He is renowned for his virtues and righteous rule, and is considered an incarnation of Lord Vishnu.

Tejahpala II was a king of the Shakambhari Chalukya Empire, ruling from around 1189 to 1192 CE. The name 'Tejahpala' is derived from Tej, meaning glory or power, and pal, meaning protector. He is remembered for his military conquests and construction of temples and forums.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's interconnected world, the name Tejeshwar continues to be cherished by Hindu families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Hindu name websites where expectant parents research meaningful names. The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.
